newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 10.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:
* Time Warner Inc has taken New Line Cinema off the market, dimming New Line chairman Bob Shaye's hopes of maintaining full autonomy. Buyers were not willing to pay the price Ted Turner wanted.

* Time Warner's Warner Bros Intl Television has signed an output deal with Britain's fledgling Channel Five. Sources said Channel Five beat out rival ITV for the deal, worth between $130 million and $150 million.
* Cuba Gooding Jr. is in final talks to play late soul singer Otis Redding in "Blaze of Glory," the story of Redding's friendship with his manager Phil Walden.
* News Corp's 20th Century Fox pushed back the release of Speed 2: Cruise Control to June 13, letting Walt Disney's Buena Vista release Con Air over the June 6 weekend.
* Tele-Communications called off plans to spin off its programming arm Liberty Media Inc, TCI Intl and Southern Satellite Systems Inc after opposition from the Internal Revenue Service.

* John Cusack is in final negotiations to join Kevin Spacey in Warner Bros.' adaptation of Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil, scheduled to begin shooting with Clint Eastwood directing next month, sources said.
